decision.explanation: The first row is unchanged. Since i/(1-i)=(-1+i)/2, the new second row is [-i+i, 5+i-2((-1+i)/2)]=[0,6]. Thus option b is correct.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Given the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} & -2 \\ -\text{i} & 5+\text{i}\end{aligned}]$, find the result of applying to $A$ the following elementary row operation:

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+\frac{\text{i}}{1-\text{i}}{R}_{1}
$$
after.worked_solution:
Let's apply the row operations to $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} & -2 \\ -\text{i} & 5+\text{i}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+\frac{\text{i}}{1-\text{i}}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} & -2 \\ -\text{i}+\frac{\text{i}(1-\text{i})}{1-\text{i}} & 5+\text{i}-\frac{2\text{i}}{1-\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} & -2 \\ -\text{i}+\text{i} & \frac{(5+\text{i})\cdot (1-\text{i})-2\text{i}}{1-\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} & -2 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the result  is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} & -2 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}].
$$

content.knowledge_point: Applying Row Operations to a Complex Matrix
content.problem:
Given the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} & -2 \\ -\text{i} & 5+\text{i}\end{aligned}]$, find the result of applying to $A$ the following elementary row operation:

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+\frac{\text{i}}{1-\text{i}}{R}_{1}
$$
content.worked_solution:
Let's apply the row operations to $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} & -2 \\ -\text{i} & 5+\text{i}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+\frac{\text{i}}{1-\text{i}}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} & -2 \\ -\text{i}+\frac{\text{i}(1-\text{i})}{1-\text{i}} & 5+\text{i}-\frac{2\text{i}}{1-\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} & -2 \\ -\text{i}+\text{i} & \frac{(5+\text{i})\cdot (1-\text{i})-2\text{i}}{1-\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} & -2 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the result  is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} & -2 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}].
$$

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
Given the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} & -2-4\text{i} \\ 3-2\text{i} & \text{i}\end{aligned}]$, find the result of applying to $A$ the following  elementary row operations:

$$
{R}_{1}=\frac{1}{1+2\text{i}}{R}_{1},\,{R}_{2}={R}_{2}+(2\text{i}-3){R}_{1}
$$
after.worked_solution:
Let's apply the row operations to $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} & -2-4\text{i} \\ 3-2\text{i} & \text{i}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{1+2\text{i}}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 3-2\text{i} & \text{i}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(2\text{i}-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 6-3\text{i}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the result is

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 6-3\text{i}\end{aligned}].
$$

content.problem:
Given the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} & -2-4\text{i} \\ 3-2\text{i} & \text{i}\end{aligned}]$, find the result of applying to $A$ the following  elementary row operations:

$$
{R}_{1}=\frac{1}{1+2\text{i}}{R}_{1},\,{R}_{2}={R}_{2}+(2\text{i}-3){R}_{1}
$$
content.worked_solution:
Let's apply the row operations to $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} & -2-4\text{i} \\ 3-2\text{i} & \text{i}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{1+2\text{i}}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 3-2\text{i} & \text{i}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(2\text{i}-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 6-3\text{i}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the result is

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 6-3\text{i}\end{aligned}].
$$
